title: The Ceiling on What May Be Put Back for a Catalogue Order
content:
What is put back onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card for a stopped catalogue order is held at a ceiling drawn from what the catalogue has actually taken from that card.

The ceiling on what may go back is the largest single transaction the catalogue has taken from the card, where the catalogue has taken more than one transaction from it; it is that transaction, where the catalogue has taken exactly one; and it is the value of the items in every other case.

**What is counted.** The transactions meant are the settled card transactions made through the catalogue on that programme's record. Both the count of them and their amounts are read from those entries.

**The three cases.**

1. More than one such transaction stands on the card: the ceiling is the largest single one of them, not their total.
2. Exactly one such transaction stands: the ceiling is that transaction.
3. No such transaction stands: the ceiling is the value of the items.

**Worked through on hypothetical entries.** A card showing catalogue transactions of 52.45 USD, 18.00 USD and 31.20 USD settled: more than one stands, so the ceiling is 52.45 USD. A card showing the 18.00 USD transaction alone: exactly one stands, so the ceiling is 18.00 USD, and a refund otherwise reckoned at 46.50 USD would be held down to 18.00 USD. A card showing no catalogue transaction at all: the ceiling is the value of the items.
